content: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It also increases paclitaxel levels through other mechanisms. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored as paclitaxel toxicity may increase when co-administered with CYP2C8 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and the starting dose of panobinostat should be reduced to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels of paricalcitol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of paroxetine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. When peginterferon alpha-2b is co-administered with CYP2D6 substrates, the therapeutic effects of these drugs may be altered. Peginterferon alpha-2b may increase or decrease the levels of CYP2D6 substrates. Caution is advised when using interferons and antiretroviral protease inhibitors together, as both can cause hepatic damage. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and the pitolisant dose should be reduced by half when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE exposure, leading to increased toxicities. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ponatinib increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir decreases the effects of pramlintide through mechanisms involving insulin resistance, which may lead to hyperglycemia. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of pravastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Prednisone decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel, micronized progesterone, and natural progesterone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of propranolol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both ritonavir and quetiapine may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and use should be avoided with drugs that prolong QT or in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and the quizartinib dose should be adjusted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. After discontinuation of the strong inhibitor, the previous quizartinib dose should be resumed. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and monitoring is necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels of rifabutin by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels of rilpivirine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ritonavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and rilpivirine should be used cautiously with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Concomitant therapy may reduce therapeutic effectiveness. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Rolapitant may increase plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates for at least 28 days following administration. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through mechanisms involving insulin resistance, which may lead to hyperglycemia. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and monitoring is necessary. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan by decreasing hepatic clearance. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and monitoring is necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Ritonavir increases the levels of sertraline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. There is an increased risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin through mechanisms involving insulin resistance, which may lead to hyperglycemia. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Stiripentol affects hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. It increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified, and monitoring is necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of streptomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir affects the metabolism of tamoxifen by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6, reducing the formation of active metabolites such as endoxifen. Decreased endoxifen levels may result in poor clinical outcomes. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
